package_info.why_malicious: These versions contain a broken access control vulnerability (CVE-2023-22515) that allows unauthenticated attackers to re-enable the setup process and create new administrator accounts, granting full control of the Confluence instance to unauthorized users.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a GET request to the /server-info.action endpoint with the setupComplete parameter set to false, which re-enables the setup process without authentication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Re-enabling the setup process should require authentication and should not be possible via a simple GET request from an unauthenticated user.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, setup endpoints are locked after initial configuration and require authentication; this behavior allows bypassing that restriction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Initial installation or legitimate reconfiguration by an authenticated administrator.

execution_context.trigger: unauthenticated HTTP request after setup re-enabled

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a POST request to the /setup/setupadministrator.action endpoint, which creates a new administrator account without requiring prior authentication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Creating administrator accounts should require authentication and should not be possible via an unauthenticated POST request.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is that only authenticated users can create admin accounts; this bypasses that control.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate setup process during initial installation.
key_indicators: Creation of new admin users outside of normal workflow

execution_context.trigger: optional unauthenticated HTTP request after admin creation

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a POST request to the /setup/finishsetup.action endpoint, which finalizes the setup process, potentially hiding evidence of exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Finalizing setup without authentication can be used to cover tracks after malicious admin creation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Setup finalization should be restricted to authenticated users and not accessible post-setup.
key_indicators: Setup process manipulation after initial installation

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a GET request to /server-info.action with setupComplete=false to re-enable the setup process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Allows access to setup endpoints without authentication.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a POST request to /setup/setupadministrator.action to create a new administrator account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains administrator access to the Confluence instance.

attack_chain.action: Attacker optionally sends a POST request to /setup/finishsetup.action to finalize the setup and potentially hide evidence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Setup process is closed, attacker retains admin access.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthenticated GET requests to /server-info.action with setupComplete parameter set to false or 0
Creation of new administrator accounts outside of normal provisioning workflows
file_indicators: Audit logs showing new admin user creation
network_indicators: Source IPs making unauthenticated requests to setup endpoints
Suspicious user agents (e.g., github.com/Chocapikk/CVE-2023-22515, Nuclei, Assetnote/1.0.0)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP access logs for unauthenticated requests to /server-info.action with setupComplete=false or 0, and POST requests to /setup/setupadministrator.action. Correlate these with the creation of new administrator accounts. Flag any such activity, especially if originating from known malicious IPs or suspicious user agents. Review admin user creation logs for unexpected or suspicious accounts.
